title: The medieval saints, again
tomorrow: what does a Church that's always in need of renewal fix first?

segments.voice: A week of the long view: sent, charity never falleth away, all things new, the turning year, fully alive, and yesterday, thinking together. Six carries. Today they get faces.

A contacts list keeps people you haven't texted in years, and you could still call any of them. Catholics talk about saints that way. Four of the old ones: Francis, a cloth merchant's son who gave everything away. Clare, who, tradition says, slipped out of her family's house at night to follow him. Dominic, a preacher who founded an order of preachers. And Catherine of Siena, who wrote fearless letters, even to a pope.
screen: `A CONTACTS LIST.` → `A RICH KID, A RUNAWAY, A PREACHER.` → `A LETTER-WRITER.`

segments.voice: Each one is a friend for a different day, and each one wears a carry from this week. Dominic sent his brothers out two by two to preach: sent. Francis called the sun his brother and the moon his sister in his Canticle of the Creatures, a man fully alive to every creature God made. Clare stayed put in one small convent for the rest of her life and kept her sisters steady with a patience that never fell away. Catherine told a pope what the Church needed, out loud and in writing, because she believed the Church could be made new. Something to tell a friend tonight: Catholics don't treat these four as statues. The Creed calls it the communion of saints: the friends who already climbed the hill are still part of the family, and they pray with the rest of us. Old friends.
screen: `DOMINIC: SENT TWO BY TWO.` · `FRANCIS: BROTHER SUN.` · `CLARE AND CATHERINE.` · `THE COMMUNION OF SAINTS.` · then, large: `OLD FRIENDS.`

segments.voice: Count four old friends on your fingers: Francis, Clare, Dominic, Catherine. Pick the one you need this week, and say the name once more, slowly. For the sit, keep that one company the way you'd sit beside a friend, no words needed.
The medieval saints. Francis, Clare, Dominic and Catherine: old friends Catholics still turn to, centuries on.
Your line: old friends. A saint is a friend who already climbed the hill. Two weeks done, see you tomorrow.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks at dinner why Catholics talk to saints who died long ago. what's a sentence a parent could say?
options: saints are old friends who finished the climb and still pray with us.

fork.reveal: Catholics honor the saints and ask their prayers, the communion of saints in the Creed; worship belongs to God alone.

chat.says: Mia and i are good again. she made me promise to call every week from Oregon. corny or real?
options: Real. Old friends stay friends across distance; Catholics say the saints are friends like that.
Corny. Friends you can't see aren't really friends; make new ones once you're there.
Real, but only until you find new people; old friends are mostly for the past.
chat.meaning: The communion of saints means friends across time and distance, still part of the family. Old friends stay close even when you can't see them.

Clare.meaning: a young woman of Assisi who followed Francis's way

Dominic.meaning: a preacher who founded the Order of Preachers

Siena.meaning: an Italian city, home of Saint Catherine

Canticle of the Creatures.meaning: Francis's song praising God for sun, moon and all creation

communion of saints.meaning: the bond of all God's people, living and dead
